category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Makes an RNN hidden state a learnable model and updates it with self-supervised gradient steps while processing the test sequence.
intelligence_leverage: Turns context processing into online learning rather than passive attention; the software opportunity is a runtime that decides what to learn, when to update, and how to roll back harmful updates.
hardware_path: Linear-time recurrent execution, but with training-like inner loops. Strong targets include fused update kernels, SRAM-resident fast weights, FPGA streaming pipelines and accelerators that combine inference and low-rank weight updates.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic: each update is polynomial; stability, selection of updates and long-horizon credit remain empirical.
maturity: Research implementation; high scientific novelty, medium product readiness

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Adds test-time training to existing transformer LLMs through a drop-in training, conversion, inference and evaluation stack.
intelligence_leverage: Important because it reduces the architecture-change barrier: runtime adaptation can become a serving feature rather than requiring an entirely new model family.
hardware_path: Requires fast parameter-delta management, isolation between users, checkpointing, mixed-precision update kernels and scheduling between decode and adaptation.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic; the central risk is non-stationary behaviour and unsafe adaptation, not worst-case complexity.
maturity: Research stack; promising bridge to deployable adaptive inference

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Uses test-time reinforcement learning on unlabeled data, deriving reward signals from test-time scaling behaviours such as consensus.
intelligence_leverage: Suggests inference can generate experience and then use that experience to update the model. This is a genuine intelligence-layer loop: propose, evaluate, learn, retry.
hardware_path: Rollout generation, verifier aggregation and online optimisation create a new datacenter workload combining inference clusters, reward services and short-burst training.
complexity_lens: NP/heuristic at the outer reasoning-search level; the RL update itself is polynomial stochastic optimisation. No complexity-class shortcut is implied.
maturity: Active research code with reproducible scripts; high upside and high safety/variance risk

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Applies reinforcement learning at test time so a model can acquire problem-specific experience while attempting a discovery task.
intelligence_leverage: Moves from “think longer” to “learn from attempts.” The valuable software layer is experiment memory, reward construction and adaptive compute allocation per problem.
hardware_path: Maps to asynchronous rollout engines, batched evaluators, simulator accelerators and high-bandwidth parameter-update paths.
complexity_lens: Often attacks hard search spaces heuristically; improvements are instance-level and do not alter NP-hard worst cases.
maturity: Early research project; strategically important but not yet a stable platform

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Adds an updatable memory component to a language model and extends it toward scalable long-term memory.
intelligence_leverage: Treats memory as model state rather than only retrieved text. This could support low-latency personalisation, continual knowledge updates and private on-device memory.
hardware_path: Memory modules may be sharded, quantised or placed on CXL/SSD tiers; write-heavy memory operations create opportunities for near-memory compute and persistent accelerator state.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic; retrieval/update policy quality is empirical and continual-learning interference is the core risk.
maturity: Research code and checkpoints; medium maturity

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Uses a retriever-pretrained MLP as an external neural memory for language models.
intelligence_leverage: Interesting middle ground between symbolic retrieval and fully modifying the base model: a learned memory can be independently trained, updated and served.
hardware_path: Dense MLP lookup/update operations can be placed on separate memory accelerators, smart NICs or CXL-attached devices; compression and batching determine economics.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic; approximate retrieval and learned generalisation rather than exact database semantics.
maturity: ICLR-era research implementation; early but concrete

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Provides a pretrained plug-and-play memory decoder intended to augment an existing LLM.
intelligence_leverage: Decouples memory capacity from the core model and may create a standard memory interface across model vendors.
hardware_path: Potential hardware path is an independent memory-serving card or DPU with compressed keys, decoder kernels and tenant isolation.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic; latency, forgetting and contamination are operational issues.
maturity: Research implementation with reusable components

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Learns how to construct agent memory using reinforcement learning rather than fixed summarisation rules.
intelligence_leverage: Memory formation becomes a trainable policy. This is more valuable than another vector store because it addresses what should be retained and in what representation.
hardware_path: The hot path is trajectory collection, memory scoring, compression and retrieval; accelerators could support streaming summarisation and hierarchical stores.
complexity_lens: NP/heuristic selection problem in practice; RL learns a policy without guaranteeing globally optimal memory.
maturity: Early research code; high conceptual leverage

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Compresses transformer key-value caches in the frequency domain to extend context windows.
intelligence_leverage: Shows that cache representations can exploit signal structure rather than using uniform token eviction or scalar quantisation.
hardware_path: Natural targets are fused FFT/DCT-like transforms, low-bit cache formats, HBM controllers and inference runtimes that schedule compressed and exact cache tiers.
complexity_lens: P-approximate: explicit quality/latency trade-off; no hard-search claim.
maturity: Research implementation; relatively close to systems integration

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Applies vector quantisation to key-value caches for high compression with improved fidelity.
intelligence_leverage: KV cache is a rapidly growing serving cost. Learned or structured codebooks create a software wedge that can later become cache-specific silicon.
hardware_path: Maps directly to lookup-table scoring, bit-packed memory, vector instructions and HBM bandwidth reduction.
complexity_lens: P-approximate with measurable reconstruction and task-quality error.
maturity: Research implementation; attractive near-term systems opportunity

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Uses a hypernetwork to convert document context into LoRA-style parameter updates that internalise facts quickly.
intelligence_leverage: Collapses retrieval context into a compact weight delta. It could create portable, cacheable “knowledge cartridges” for models and agents.
hardware_path: Requires fast hypernetwork inference, delta loading, multiplexed adapter memory and secure per-tenant parameter state. FPGA or DPU adapter managers are plausible.
complexity_lens: P/probabilistic; generated updates are approximate and require validation against hallucination or interference.
maturity: ICML 2026 research implementation with weights; high novelty

category: Adaptive memory and test-time learning
novelty: Generates long chains of thought with a small context window by recursively deleting intermediate thoughts no longer needed.
intelligence_leverage: Treats reasoning memory as garbage-collected state. The broader idea is an operating system for cognitive workspace, not simply a longer context window.
hardware_path: Hardware leverage comes from lower KV traffic and from runtime support for state compaction, dependency tracking and selective recomputation.
complexity_lens: P/heuristic; determining what can be safely discarded is an approximate relevance problem.
maturity: Early research implementation; strong systems idea

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: A fully open effort to reproduce reasoning-model training recipes, including data, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
intelligence_leverage: Lowers the barrier to experimenting with reward design and reasoning traces, making the training stack itself an extensible intelligence layer.
hardware_path: Large-scale rollout, reward verification and distributed optimisation favour tightly integrated inference/training clusters and specialised verifier services.
complexity_lens: NP/heuristic reasoning search layered on polynomial training kernels.
maturity: Mature open research ecosystem; strong platform value

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Open implementation of large-scale reasoning-oriented reinforcement learning from a base model.
intelligence_leverage: Useful because it exposes the recipe, parameters, data and weights needed to study emergent verification and search behaviours.
hardware_path: Same hardware pattern as RLHF but more rollout-heavy: inference throughput, long sequences, reward checks and checkpoint churn dominate.
complexity_lens: Hard reasoning tasks remain hard; RL changes the search policy and practical success distribution.
maturity: Research platform with released assets

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Minimal reproduction showing small models can develop verification/search behaviours through reinforcement learning on constrained tasks.
intelligence_leverage: A compact test bed for studying which parts of reasoning emergence require scale and which come from environment and reward structure.
hardware_path: Excellent FPGA/small-cluster research target because experiments are small enough to profile end-to-end and co-design rollout plus update hardware.
complexity_lens: Structured task environments; no general NP breakthrough.
maturity: Educational/research implementation; original repo is largely superseded by veRL

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Distributed reinforcement-learning framework for LLMs with flexible training and inference backends.
intelligence_leverage: Potentially becomes the control plane for experience-based model improvement: rollouts, rewards, policy updates and agentic environments.
hardware_path: Strong datacenter leverage: disaggregated inference/training, sequence parallelism, checkpoint movement, network topology and GPU utilisation.
complexity_lens: P stochastic optimisation with heuristic policy search.
maturity: Fast-moving infrastructure project; high practical relevance

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Framework for training agents with reinforcement learning while integrating with multiple agent frameworks and benchmark environments.
intelligence_leverage: Makes agent behaviour rather than isolated text generation the trainable object.
hardware_path: Needs trace capture, asynchronous experience queues, reward execution and multi-GPU optimisation; DPUs can isolate environments and telemetry.
complexity_lens: Agent planning may be combinatorial; RL supplies heuristics and policies.
maturity: Emerging framework; promising interoperability

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Open distributed RLHF and reinforcement-learning stack for large models.
intelligence_leverage: Provides reusable infrastructure beneath many reasoning and alignment experiments, reducing the cost of testing new algorithms.
hardware_path: Datacenter-scale scheduling, ZeRO/FSDP, inference engines and high-speed collectives are the main hardware interfaces.
complexity_lens: P stochastic optimisation; reward optimisation does not guarantee global behavioural properties.
maturity: Established open-source training stack

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Environment microservice framework for asynchronous reinforcement learning with language models.
intelligence_leverage: Separates environments from trainers through a trajectory interface, enabling a marketplace of executable learning tasks.
hardware_path: Environment services can run on CPU pools, simulators, browsers or accelerators while GPUs remain saturated with generation/training.
complexity_lens: Often wraps hard interactive tasks; reward and policy learning are heuristic.
maturity: Active and community-oriented; strong intelligence-infrastructure thesis

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Uses open software-evolution data and rule-based rewards to train language models for real software engineering.
intelligence_leverage: Transforms repositories, diffs and test outcomes into an experience stream. This can compound with every open-source change and every customer codebase.
hardware_path: Requires sandbox fleets, incremental builds, test execution and diff evaluators; CPUs and storage can dominate more than GPU FLOPs.
complexity_lens: Software repair is combinatorial and program correctness is undecidable in general; tests provide partial verifiers.
maturity: NeurIPS 2025 research code; strategically important

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: General agentic RL framework spanning terminal, GUI, software engineering and tool-use settings.
intelligence_leverage: Attempts to optimise multiple components of an agent in a closed loop rather than training only the base model.
hardware_path: Calls for heterogeneous clusters: GPUs for policy models, CPU/browser farms for environments, storage for traces and fast networking for asynchronous feedback.
complexity_lens: Heuristic optimisation over long-horizon tasks; no global guarantees.
maturity: ICML 2026-stage research project; high ambition

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Standard interface for isolated agentic execution environments using Gym-style APIs and deployable packaging.
intelligence_leverage: Could become an ABI for agent experience, analogous to what Gym did for classic RL but with richer tools, databases and sandboxes.
hardware_path: Strong DPU/virtualisation opportunity: secure environment execution, network policy, snapshotting and deterministic replay.
complexity_lens: The environment API is P infrastructure; tasks inside may be arbitrarily hard.
maturity: Active ecosystem infrastructure with broad integrations

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Synthesises executable SQL-backed tool-use environments for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning.
intelligence_leverage: Environment generation tackles a central bottleneck: agents need abundant interactive experience, not only static text.
hardware_path: Database-backed environments, verification and MCP services can scale horizontally on CPU/storage clusters while GPU workers train policies.
complexity_lens: Generating useful curricula is heuristic; task execution is mostly polynomial database/program work.
maturity: ICML 2026 research release with datasets and environments

category: Reasoning, reinforcement learning and agent training
novelty: Self-evolving agents from zero curated data using a curriculum agent and an executor agent that co-evolve through tool-integrated reasoning.
intelligence_leverage: The important novelty is automatic curriculum creation: the system generates its own frontier rather than waiting for human datasets.
hardware_path: Compute shifts toward large volumes of verified rollouts, tool execution and curriculum filtering. Efficient schedulers and verifier accelerators matter.
complexity_lens: Open-ended search is heuristic and potentially unbounded; gains are empirical.
maturity: Early research release; high upside and high evaluation risk

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: A coding agent repeatedly evaluates itself, modifies its own codebase and retains changes that improve benchmark performance.
intelligence_leverage: A clean experimental substrate for recursive software improvement with an explicit archive and evaluation loop.
hardware_path: Sandboxed build/test farms, benchmark caching and code-diff execution dominate. Hardware acceleration is secondary until many parallel variants are evaluated.
complexity_lens: Program search is enormous and generally intractable; evolutionary/agent search is heuristic and benchmark-bound.
maturity: Research prototype; useful for controlled experiments

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Open-ended system that modifies its own agent code and empirically validates changes on coding benchmarks.
intelligence_leverage: Combines self-reference with evolutionary archives rather than requiring every new version to descend from only the current best.
hardware_path: Scales through parallel sandboxes, evaluation caching and heterogeneous model calls; secure execution is essential.
complexity_lens: Heuristic search over programs; empirical improvement does not imply formal self-correctness.
maturity: Research code; conceptually significant and operationally risky

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Evolutionary coding agent inspired by AlphaEvolve, using language models to mutate and optimise programs against measurable objectives.
intelligence_leverage: Makes algorithm and implementation search accessible as a reusable open framework. The moat opportunity is evaluator libraries and workload-specific archives.
hardware_path: Ideal for hardware co-design: generated kernels can be benchmarked on GPUs, CPUs, FPGAs or simulators; evaluation parallelism is the key resource.
complexity_lens: Heuristic program synthesis over NP-hard/undecidable spaces; correctness must come from tests or proofs.
maturity: Active community project; high practical experimentation value

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Open-ended, sample-efficient program evolution framework aimed at scientific discovery and optimisation.
intelligence_leverage: Focuses on maintaining diversity and extracting more value per expensive evaluation, a critical issue in real scientific search.
hardware_path: Works well with distributed experiment schedulers, GPU kernel benchmarks, simulators and lab automation.
complexity_lens: Heuristic evolutionary search; can attack NP-hard design spaces without changing worst-case complexity.
maturity: 2026 active research release; strong discovery platform candidate

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Lets an agent repeatedly modify a compact language-model training codebase, run short experiments and keep improvements.
intelligence_leverage: A minimal example of “research organisation as code”: the human writes the research constitution and the agent executes the experimental loop.
hardware_path: Single-GPU baseline, but naturally scales to experiment fleets, scheduler-aware early stopping and shared result memory.
complexity_lens: Heuristic search over training programs and hyperparameters.
maturity: Compact experimental project; high educational and cultural influence

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: End-to-end scientific research system using agentic tree search to generate hypotheses, run experiments, analyse results and draft papers.
intelligence_leverage: Expands the unit of automation from a code task to an entire research programme with explicit branching and experiment management.
hardware_path: Requires sandboxed GPU experiments, literature retrieval, plotting, LaTeX and tree-search scheduling. Secure execution and cost-aware pruning are core infrastructure.
complexity_lens: Research planning and experiment selection are combinatorial and heuristic; peer acceptance is not equivalent to truth.
maturity: Advanced research prototype with real artefacts; requires stringent oversight

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Plan-and-act autonomous research agent with an outer planning loop and inner act-reflect loop.
intelligence_leverage: Provides a general controller specialised through research tools and prompts; useful as a transparent baseline for autonomous discovery systems.
hardware_path: CPU-heavy tools, retrieval and experimental code execution surround model inference. Traceability and replay are more important than raw decode speed.
complexity_lens: Heuristic planning over open-ended action spaces.
maturity: Active research agent; moderate maturity

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Open framework for multi-agent autonomous research from literature review through hypothesis generation, experiments and manuscript production.
intelligence_leverage: Treats scientific work as a collaborative agent workflow and provides a user-facing research operating environment.
hardware_path: Opportunity lies in workflow orchestration, provenance stores, sandboxing, multi-model routing and local/private execution.
complexity_lens: Heuristic orchestration; scientific validity still requires independent replication.
maturity: Fast-moving open-source product/research hybrid

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Automatically generates and optimises agent workflows using Monte Carlo tree search over code-represented workflows.
intelligence_leverage: Moves agent engineering from hand-written prompts and graphs toward automated architecture search.
hardware_path: Workflow evaluation is embarrassingly parallel and can exploit model routers, caching and FPGA/ASIC inference when workloads stabilise.
complexity_lens: MCTS is heuristic search; optimal workflow discovery is combinatorial.
maturity: ICLR 2025 research implementation; important agent-compiler direction

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Collection of research projects on agents that improve web reasoning, curricula or tool-use behaviour.
intelligence_leverage: Useful as a laboratory for multiple self-evolution mechanisms rather than a single monolithic agent.
hardware_path: Scales on browser/sandbox fleets and asynchronous trace stores; evaluation quality is the limiting resource.
complexity_lens: Heuristic learning and search.
maturity: Research collection under active development

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: End-to-end multi-agent workflow supporting literature review, experimentation and report writing with human involvement.
intelligence_leverage: A practical reference architecture for decomposing scientific work into specialised roles and shared artefacts.
hardware_path: Local or cloud model serving, literature indexes, sandboxed Python and reproducible project storage are the main systems layers.
complexity_lens: Heuristic planning; no guarantee of novelty or correctness.
maturity: Usable research workflow with community adoption

category: Self-improving software and autonomous research
novelty: Local-first autonomous research studio that preserves findings memory, runs iterative experiments and produces paper-oriented outputs.
intelligence_leverage: The local-first and persistent-project design is valuable: intelligence growth depends on durable experimental memory, not isolated chats.
hardware_path: Maps to workstation/GPU scheduling, experiment databases, Bayesian optimisation and private local models.
complexity_lens: Experiment selection is heuristic; statistical controls are required to avoid overfitting the research loop.
maturity: Active 2026 project; product-like usability with research ambitions

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Programming language and theorem prover with a small trusted kernel and extensible metaprogramming system.
intelligence_leverage: Provides a machine-checkable substrate for mathematical knowledge, software specifications and proof-producing agents.
hardware_path: Proof checking is highly parallel at the project level; tactic search can use GPUs, while the small kernel remains CPU-friendly and auditable.
complexity_lens: Proof checking is decidable for submitted terms; proof search can be combinatorial or undecidable in broad settings.
maturity: Mature foundational platform and active ecosystem

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Large collaborative library of formalised mathematics for Lean 4.
intelligence_leverage: Acts as structured, verified training data and a compositional knowledge base for theorem-proving systems.
hardware_path: Indexing, premise retrieval, incremental builds and distributed checking are the main acceleration opportunities.
complexity_lens: Verification is polynomial in proof-term size under the kernel; discovering proofs remains hard.
maturity: Large mature community asset

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: End-to-end framework for extracting data, training, evaluating and deploying AI theorem provers for Lean 4.
intelligence_leverage: Bridges formal libraries and machine learning with reproducible environments and interfaces.
hardware_path: Supports GPU premise/proof models plus CPU proof checking; retrieval and search scheduling can be independently accelerated.
complexity_lens: Proof search is combinatorial; kernel verification supplies exact certificates.
maturity: Research infrastructure with strong reuse potential

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Integrates language-model assistance directly into Lean theorem proving.
intelligence_leverage: Shows how neural suggestions can remain subordinate to a trusted formal checker, a strong model for safe code and scientific agents.
hardware_path: On-device or server inference can propose tactics; the Lean kernel validates them. Quantised small models and retrieval accelerators are natural.
complexity_lens: Heuristic proposal plus exact checking.
maturity: Usable research tool integrated with Lean

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Machine-to-machine interaction system for Lean 4 designed for automated proof agents.
intelligence_leverage: Provides a lower-level control interface than human IDE tooling, enabling tree search, branching and structured proof-state manipulation.
hardware_path: Search workers can run in parallel while shared proof-state caches and CPU kernels verify candidates.
complexity_lens: Combinatorial proof search with exact certificate checking.
maturity: Research infrastructure; strategically important interface layer

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Open theorem-proving model and data pipeline that formalises natural-language mathematics into Lean and generates proofs.
intelligence_leverage: Combines formalisation and proof generation, attacking both the translation bottleneck and proof search.
hardware_path: GPU inference and retrieval produce candidate statements/proofs; Lean checking provides a cheap trusted filter.
complexity_lens: Heuristic search with exact proof verification; formalisation correctness still requires semantic review.
maturity: Open models and code; frontier research

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Uses proof-assistant feedback, reinforcement learning and Monte Carlo tree search for Lean theorem proving.
intelligence_leverage: Demonstrates a powerful closed loop: generate proof steps, receive exact checker feedback and improve search.
hardware_path: Long batched proof rollouts, retrieval and CPU checker farms create a heterogeneous acceleration opportunity.
complexity_lens: MCTS/RL tackle hard proof search; accepted proofs are exact certificates.
maturity: Open research model and code

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Predicts proof progress and uses the signal to guide neural theorem-proving search.
intelligence_leverage: A learned progress metric can reduce wasted search, analogous to value functions in planning.
hardware_path: Value-model inference can be batched on GPUs; proof states can be cached and verified on CPUs.
complexity_lens: Heuristic guidance over combinatorial search; exact final checking.
maturity: Minimal research implementation; promising component

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Combines language-model scientific priors, program skeletons and evolutionary search for symbolic equation discovery.
intelligence_leverage: Produces interpretable equations instead of only predictions and can inject domain knowledge into search.
hardware_path: Candidate evaluation is massively parallel across CPU/GPU simulation; symbolic simplification and constant fitting are accelerator targets.
complexity_lens: Symbolic regression is combinatorial/NP-hard in common formulations; the method is heuristic with empirical validation.
maturity: ICLR 2025 oral code release

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Benchmark of scientific equation discovery designed to test reasoning beyond memorised textbook forms.
intelligence_leverage: Critical because intelligence-layer progress needs adversarial, transformation-based benchmarks rather than easy recycled equations.
hardware_path: Primarily evaluation infrastructure; scalable candidate execution and symbolic equivalence checking are useful.

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Guides symbolic regression using minimum-description-length objectives rather than prediction error alone.
intelligence_leverage: Aligns discovery with compact explanatory laws, reducing overfit equations that merely interpolate data.
hardware_path: Search and scoring can be distributed; bit-level description-length calculations and symbolic canonicalisation are cheap verification layers.
complexity_lens: Combinatorial search with an information-theoretic objective; heuristic guidance.

category: Formal reasoning and machine-assisted discovery
novelty: Lean framework for neural-network specification, execution and verification.

novelty: Multimodal molecular structure-prediction model covering proteins, small molecules, DNA, RNA and modifications.

novelty: Diffusion-based generative approach to molecular docking that predicts ligand poses in protein pockets.

novelty: Generative diffusion model for designing protein backbones and structures under constraints.

novelty: Differentiable molecular-dynamics library built around JAX transformations and accelerator execution.
